# Econometrics

Strategy (thesis, Chapters 4–5): (1) descriptives and within/between variance (Table 2), (2) pooled OLS, RE, one-way FE, two-way FE and Mundlak / correlated random effects (Table 3, Appendix A1–A2), (3) classical Hausman and robust Mundlak tests, Wooldridge and Pesaran CD diagnostics (Table 4), (4) within vs between associations (Table 5), (5) robustness checks and industry placebo (Appendix A3–A4).

All inference uses standard errors clustered by country (Arellano, 1987), robust to heteroskedasticity and serial correlation. Driscoll–Kraay SEs (also robust to cross-sectional dependence) are used as a robustness check.

Interpretation: outcomes are in logs and urban regressors in percentage points, so 100 × β = % change in per-capita emissions for a one-percentage-point increase. The coefficients on `ln_cons` and `ln_density` are elasticities.

Table 1 (literature overview) is made directly in Word; Figure 1 is produced in `03_figures.qmd`.

BLOCK 1 — Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup-econometrics
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(plm)        # panel models, Hausman, Wooldridge, Pesaran CD, Driscoll-Kraay (vcovSCC)
library(lmtest)     # coeftest()
library(sandwich)   # cluster-robust variance
library(car)        # linearHypothesis() for the robust Mundlak test
library(flextable)  # thesis tables (booktabs style)
library(officer)    # line styles for flextable

df_model <- read_csv(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_wdi_panel.csv"))
```

BLOCK 2 — Variables, Mundlak means, lags, panel index

```{r}
#| label: panel-and-mundlak
#| message: false

# Main regressors: URB, PRIM, LAS^u, ln CONS, ln DENS
x_main <- c("urb_rate", "population_largest_city_pct_urb", "pop_over_1M_pct_urb", "ln_cons", "ln_density")

# Robustness: original WDI measure of 1M+ agglomerations (LAS^t, % of TOTAL population)
x_alt  <- c("urb_rate", "population_largest_city_pct_urb", "urban_population_over_1M", "ln_cons", "ln_density")

# Robustness: urban-structure variables lagged (t-1); consumption and density stay contemporaneous
x_lag  <- c("lag_urb_rate", "lag_population_largest_city_pct_urb", "lag_pop_over_1M_pct_urb", "ln_cons", "ln_density")

df_m <- df_model %>%
  arrange(country_code, year) %>%
  group_by(country_code) %>%
  mutate(
    # Mundlak: country means of the EXACT regressors (mean of the log, not log of the mean)
    across(all_of(x_main), mean, .names = "m_{.col}"),
    across(c(urb_rate, population_largest_city_pct_urb, pop_over_1M_pct_urb),
           ~ dplyr::lag(.x), .names = "lag_{.col}")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

pdata <- pdata.frame(df_m, index = c("country_code", "year"))
```

BLOCK 3 — Countries with suspicious jumps in the urbanization rate (thesis, Section 3.4)

A jump of many points in a few years in an OECD country usually reflects a change in the national definition of "urban", not real urbanization. The countries identified here are excluded in robustness column (5) of Table A3.

```{r}
#| label: urb-rate-jumps

df_m %>%
  group_by(country_code, country_name) %>%
  summarise(change_2000_2019 = last(urb_rate) - first(urb_rate),
            max_yearly_jump  = max(abs(diff(urb_rate))),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(change_2000_2019)) %>%
  head(8)

reclass_countries <- c("TUR", "JPN", "NLD", "CRI")
pdata_noreclass <- pdata.frame(filter(df_m, !country_code %in% reclass_countries),
                               index = c("country_code", "year"))
```

BLOCK 4 — Primacy and country size (thesis, Section 6.3)

```{r}
#| label: primacy-country-size

# Average primacy and average population by country, 2000-2019
prim_pays <- df_m %>%
  group_by(country_code) %>%
  summarise(prim    = mean(population_largest_city_pct_urb),
            pop_mio = mean(pop_total) / 1e6) %>%
  arrange(desc(prim))

print(prim_pays, n = 35)

# Cross-country correlation between country size (log population) and primacy
cor(log(prim_pays$pop_mio), prim_pays$prim)
```

BLOCK 5 — Descriptive statistics and within/between variance decomposition (Table 2)

```{r}
#| label: descriptives

vars_desc <- c("co2_transport_pc", "co2_building_pc", x_main)

# sd_within    : deviations from the country mean (one-way, descriptive)
# sd_within_tw : deviations from country AND year means (two-way demeaning, exact because
#                the panel is balanced). This is the variation the two-way FE model uses,
#                so it is the "typical within change" used for effect sizes (Figure 1).
decomp <- df_m %>%
  select(country_code, year, all_of(vars_desc)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(country_code, year), names_to = "variable") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(grand_mean = mean(value)) %>%
  group_by(variable, country_code) %>%
  mutate(country_mean = mean(value), within_dev = value - country_mean) %>%
  group_by(variable, year) %>%
  mutate(year_mean = mean(value),
         within_dev_tw = value - country_mean - year_mean + grand_mean) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    mean         = mean(value),
    sd_overall   = sd(value),
    sd_between   = sd(tapply(value, country_code, mean)),
    sd_within    = sd(within_dev),
    sd_within_tw = sd(within_dev_tw),
    min          = min(value),
    max          = max(value),
    share_within = sd_within^2 / sd_overall^2
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

decomp

# Extremes of per capita emissions quoted in Section 5.1
df_m %>%
  select(country_code, year, co2_transport_pc, co2_building_pc) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(country_code, year)) %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  filter(value %in% range(value))
```

BLOCK 6 — Models

```{r}
#| label: models

make_f <- function(y, x, extra = NULL) reformulate(c(x, extra), response = y)

# Cluster-robust (by country) variance matrix
vc_cl <- function(m) vcovHC(m, method = "arellano", type = "HC1", cluster = "group")

# Main model sequence for one outcome (Section 4.2)
fit_main <- function(y, x = x_main, data = pdata) {
  list(
    "Pooled OLS"        = plm(make_f(y, x), data, model = "pooling"),   # no country, no year effects
    "RE"                = plm(make_f(y, x, "factor(year)"), data, model = "random"),
    "FE (country)"      = plm(make_f(y, x), data, model = "within", effect = "individual"),
    "FE (country+year)" = plm(make_f(y, x), data, model = "within", effect = "twoways"),
    "Mundlak / CRE"     = plm(make_f(y, x, c(paste0("m_", x), "factor(year)")), data, model = "random")
  )
}

fe_tw <- function(y, x = x_main, data = pdata) plm(make_f(y, x), data, model = "within", effect = "twoways")

m_tr <- fit_main("ln_co2_transport_pc")
m_bu <- fit_main("ln_co2_building_pc")
```

BLOCK 7 — Specification and diagnostic tests (Table 4)

```{r}
#| label: tests

# (a) Classical Hausman (assumes homoskedastic, non-autocorrelated errors)
haus <- function(m) phtest(m[["FE (country+year)"]], m[["RE"]])

# (b) Robust Hausman = Mundlak Wald test with clustered SEs: H0 = all country means jointly zero
mundlak_test <- function(m) {
  means <- grep("^m_", names(coef(m)), value = TRUE)
  linearHypothesis(m, paste(means, "= 0"), vcov. = vc_cl(m), test = "Chisq")
}

# (c) Wooldridge serial correlation (one-way FE) and Pesaran CD (two-way FE)
diag_tests <- function(y) {
  fe1 <- plm(make_f(y, x_main), pdata, model = "within", effect = "individual")
  list(wool = pwartest(fe1),
       pes  = pcdtest(fe_tw(y), test = "cd"))
}

h_tr <- haus(m_tr); h_bu <- haus(m_bu)
w_tr <- mundlak_test(m_tr[["Mundlak / CRE"]]); w_bu <- mundlak_test(m_bu[["Mundlak / CRE"]])
d_tr <- diag_tests("ln_co2_transport_pc"); d_bu <- diag_tests("ln_co2_building_pc")

# Degrees of freedom of the Hausman test (check: should be 5)
cat("Hausman df:", h_tr$parameter, "(transport),", h_bu$parameter, "(buildings)\n")

# Sanity check: Mundlak within coefficients must equal the two-way FE estimates
for (m in list(m_tr, m_bu)) {
  print(round(cbind(FE_twoways = coef(m[["FE (country+year)"]])[x_main],
                    Mundlak    = coef(m[["Mundlak / CRE"]])[x_main]), 5))
}
```

BLOCK 8 — Robustness checks, placebo and long differences (Appendix A3–A4)

Long differences: urban structure changes slowly and the yearly series are partly interpolated, so only the change over the whole period is used: one observation per country, Δy = α + Δx'β + ε, with start and end values as 3-year averages (2000–02, 2017–19). The constant captures the common trend (the equivalent of year effects). N = 35, HC1 robust SEs, results read as indicative.

```{r}
#| label: robustness

# Table A3, columns (1)-(5)
robust_models <- function(y) {
  base <- fe_tw(y)
  list(
    "Baseline"                 = base,
    "Driscoll-Kraay SE"        = base,
    "Urban vars lagged (t-1)"  = fe_tw(y, x_lag),
    "LAS as % of total pop."   = fe_tw(y, x_alt),
    "Excl. TUR, JPN, NLD, CRI" = fe_tw(y, x_main, pdata_noreclass)
  )
}

robust_vcov <- function(ms) {
  v <- map(ms, vc_cl)
  v[["Driscoll-Kraay SE"]] <- vcovSCC(ms[["Driscoll-Kraay SE"]], maxlag = 2)   # m(T) = floor(4(T/100)^(2/9)) = 2
  v
}

r_tr <- robust_models("ln_co2_transport_pc")
r_bu <- robust_models("ln_co2_building_pc")

# Table A3, column (6): long differences
sector_y <- c("Transport" = "ln_co2_transport_pc", "Buildings" = "ln_co2_building_pc")
ld_vars  <- c(unname(sector_y), x_main)

df_ld <- df_m %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(year <= 2002 ~ "start", year >= 2017 ~ "end")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(period)) %>%
  group_by(country_code, period) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(ld_vars), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(ld_vars), names_to = "variable") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(d = end - start) %>%
  select(country_code, variable, d) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = d, names_prefix = "d_")

m_ld <- map(set_names(paste0("d_", sector_y), names(sector_y)),
            ~ lm(reformulate(paste0("d_", x_main), response = .x), data = df_ld))

# Table A4: industry placebo (same two-way FE specification)
m_plac <- list(c1 = fe_tw("ln_co2_transport_pc"),
               c2 = fe_tw("ln_co2_building_pc"),
               c3 = fe_tw("ln_co2_industry_pc"))
```

Only three horizontal rules (thick top, thin under the header, thick bottom), no vertical lines, Times New Roman, compact line spacing. Numbering follows the thesis:

|----|----|----|
| Table 1 | Overview of the reviewed empirical literature (made in Word) | 2.3 |

| Table 3 | Two-way FE, transport and buildings, with Hausman and Mundlak tests | 5.2 |
| Table 4 | Specification and diagnostic tests | 5.3 |
| Table 5 | Within vs between vs gap (Mundlak), both sectors | 5.4 |

Each table is saved as its own .docx in `output/tables/thesis/`: open it, copy the table, paste into the thesis with "Keep source formatting".

```{r}
#| label: thesis-tables
#| message: false

dir.create(here("output", "tables"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
out_thesis <- function(f) here("output", "tables", f)
unlink(list.files(here("output", "tables"), full.names = TRUE))  # remove old exports

## ---------- 1. Labels and formatting helpers ----------

labels <- c(
  "urb_rate"                            = "Urbanization rate (%)",
  "population_largest_city_pct_urb"     = "Primacy, PRIM (% of urban pop.)",
  "pop_over_1M_pct_urb"                 = "Large-agglomeration share, LAS (% of urban pop.)",
  "ln_cons"                             = "ln household consumption p.c.",
  "ln_density"                          = "ln population density",
  "m_urb_rate"                          = "Mean: urbanization rate",
  "m_population_largest_city_pct_urb"   = "Mean: PRIM",
  "m_pop_over_1M_pct_urb"               = "Mean: LAS",
  "m_ln_cons"                           = "Mean: ln consumption",
  "m_ln_density"                        = "Mean: ln density"
)
lab3 <- c(urb  = "Urbanization rate (%)",
          prim = "Primacy, PRIM (% of urban pop.)",
          m1   = "Large-agglomeration share, LAS (% of urban pop.)")

# Numbers with 3 decimals and a real minus sign
fmt_num <- function(x, d = 3) str_replace(formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d), "^-", "−")
fmt_p   <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
star_of <- function(p) case_when(p < .01 ~ "***", p < .05 ~ "**", p < .1 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")
r2_of   <- function(m) if (inherits(m, "plm")) summary(m)$r.squared[["rsq"]] else summary(m)$r.squared
fmt_chi <- function(stat, p) paste0(formatC(stat, format = "f", digits = 1), star_of(p))
fmt_test <- function(stat, p, d = 1) sprintf("%s (p %s)", fmt_num(stat, d),
                                              ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", fmt_p(p))))

STARS_NOTE <- "* p < 0.1, ** p < 0.05, *** p < 0.01."

# Regression block: two lines per variable (coefficient + stars, SE in parentheses).
#   models  : named list of models (names = internal column names)
#   vcovs   : list of variance matrices, same order
#   rows    : row keys; row_labels: named vector key -> printed label
#   term_map: optional list (one per model) mapping row key -> coefficient name,
#             needed when columns use different variables (lags, alt. measure, long differences)
reg_block <- function(models, vcovs, rows, row_labels, term_map = NULL) {
  if (is.null(term_map)) term_map <- rep(list(setNames(rows, rows)), length(models))
  ct <- map2(models, vcovs, ~ coeftest(.x, vcov. = .y))
  cell <- function(j, key, what) {
    t <- unname(term_map[[j]][key]); x <- ct[[j]]
    if (is.na(t) || !t %in% rownames(x)) return("")
    if (what == "est") paste0(fmt_num(x[t, 1]), star_of(x[t, 4])) else paste0("(", fmt_num(x[t, 2]), ")")
  }
  map_dfr(rows, function(k) {
    est <- map_chr(seq_along(models), ~ cell(.x, k, "est"))
    se  <- map_chr(seq_along(models), ~ cell(.x, k, "se"))
    vals <- map(seq_along(models), ~ c(est[.x], se[.x])) |> set_names(names(models))
    tibble(Variable = c(unname(row_labels[k]), ""), !!!vals)
  })
}

# One extra line (e.g. "Observations") in a table with columns `cols`
stat_row <- function(label, values, cols) {
  as_tibble(as.list(setNames(c(label, as.character(values)), c("Variable", cols))))
}

# Empty line used as a panel title ("Panel A: Transport")
panel_row <- function(title, cols) stat_row(title, rep("", length(cols)), cols)

# Booktabs style: call AFTER all rows / header rows are added
style_booktabs <- function(ft, caption, note, panel_i = NULL, rule_i = NULL, widths = NULL) {
  thick <- fp_border(width = 1.5); thin <- fp_border(width = 0.75)
  ft <- ft |>
    border_remove() |>
    hline_top(border = thick, part = "header") |>
    hline_bottom(border = thin, part = "header") |>
    hline_bottom(border = thick, part = "body") |>
    font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
    fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
    align(align = "center", part = "all") |>
    align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") |>
    padding(padding.top = 0, padding.bottom = 0, part = "all") |>
    line_spacing(space = 1, part = "all")
  for (i in rule_i)  ft <- hline(ft, i = i, border = thin, part = "body")      # thin rule before the stats lines
  for (i in panel_i) ft <- ft |> merge_at(i = i, j = 1:ncol_keys(ft), part = "body") |>
                                  italic(i = i, part = "body")
  ft |>
    add_footer_lines(paste("Notes:", note)) |>
    fontsize(size = 8, part = "footer") |>
    align(align = "left", part = "footer") |>
    set_caption(caption = caption) |>
    autofit() -> ft
  # Fixed column widths (in inches) for wide tables, so they fit the page (A4, 1-inch margins = 6.3 in)
  if (!is.null(widths)) ft <- ft |> width(j = seq_along(widths), width = widths) |>
                              set_table_properties(layout = "fixed")
  ft
}

                 "Mundlak: Wald test that the country means are jointly zero, with SE clustered by country (robust Hausman).",
                 "Critical values of χ²(5): 9.24 (10%), 11.07 (5%), 15.09 (1%).",
                 "Wooldridge: test for serial correlation in one-way FE residuals.",

ft_tests

## ---------- Table 5 (5.4): within vs between vs gap (Mundlak) ----------
# Three columns per sector: within = beta (equal to the two-way FE estimate),
# between = beta + gamma, gap = gamma (coefficient on the country mean).

wb_cols <- function(m) {
  V <- vc_cl(m); cf <- coef(m)   # "cf", not "b": tibble() below creates a column named b
  cell <- function(est, se) {
    p <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se))
    c(paste0(fmt_num(est), star_of(p)), paste0("(", fmt_num(se), ")"))
  }
  map_dfr(x_main, function(x) {
    mx <- paste0("m_", x)
    w_cell <- cell(cf[[x]],             sqrt(V[x, x]))
    b_cell <- cell(cf[[x]] + cf[[mx]],  sqrt(V[x, x] + V[mx, mx] + 2 * V[x, mx]))
    g_cell <- cell(cf[[mx]],            sqrt(V[mx, mx]))
    tibble(w = w_cell, b = b_cell, g = g_cell)
  })
}

wb_tr <- wb_cols(m_tr[["Mundlak / CRE"]])
wb_bu <- wb_cols(m_bu[["Mundlak / CRE"]])

t_wb <- tibble(Variable = as.vector(rbind(unname(labels[x_main]), "")),
               tr_w = wb_tr$w, tr_b = wb_tr$b, tr_g = wb_tr$g,
               bu_w = wb_bu$w, bu_b = wb_bu$b, bu_g = wb_bu$g)

ft_wb <- flextable(t_wb) |>
  set_header_labels(values = list(Variable = "",
                                  tr_w = "Within (β)", tr_b = "Between (β+γ)", tr_g = "Gap (γ)",
                                  bu_w = "Within (β)", bu_b = "Between (β+γ)", bu_g = "Gap (γ)")) |>
  add_header_row(values = c("", "Transport", "Buildings"), colwidths = c(1, 3, 3)) |>
  style_booktabs(
    caption = "Table 5: Within-country versus between-country associations (Mundlak model)",
    note = paste("Correlated random effects (Mundlak) model with year effects and country means of all regressors.",
                 "Within = β (equal to the two-way FE estimate); between = β + γ;",
                 "gap = γ, the coefficient on the country mean: a significant γ means that the within and",
                 "between associations differ. Joint test of γ = 0: Table 4.",
                 "Standard errors clustered by country in parentheses.", STARS_NOTE),
    widths = c(1.6, 0.75, 0.85, 0.7, 0.75, 0.85, 0.7)) |>
  hline(i = 1, j = 2:7, border = fp_border(width = 0.75), part = "header")
ft_wb

## ---------- Appendix Tables A1–A2: all estimators ----------

full_table <- function(m, caption) {
  ms <- set_names(m, paste0("c", seq_along(m)))
  cols <- names(ms)
  keys <- c(x_main, paste0("m_", x_main))
  body <- reg_block(ms, map(ms, vc_cl), keys, labels)
  t <- bind_rows(
    body,
    stat_row("Country effects",    c("No", "Random", "Fixed", "Fixed", "Means"), cols),
    stat_row("Year fixed effects", c("No", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes"), cols),
    stat_row("Observations",       map_int(ms, nobs), cols),
    stat_row("R²",                 fmt_num(map_dbl(ms, r2_of)), cols)
  )
  flextable(t) |>
    set_header_labels(values = list(Variable = "", c1 = "Pooled OLS", c2 = "RE", c3 = "FE (country)",
                                    c4 = "Two-way FE", c5 = "Mundlak")) |>
    add_header_row(values = c("", paste0("(", 1:5, ")")), colwidths = rep(1, 6)) |>
    style_booktabs(
      caption = caption,
      note = paste("Dependent variable: ln per capita CO₂ emissions. Standard errors clustered by country in parentheses.",
                   "Column (4) corresponds to Table 3.",
                   "In column (5), the \"Mean\" rows are the coefficients on the country means (γ); the between effect is β + γ (Table 5).",
                   "R² values are not comparable across estimators.", STARS_NOTE),
      rule_i = nrow(body))
}

ft_A1 <- full_table(m_tr, "Table A1: Transport emissions, all estimators")
ft_A2 <- full_table(m_bu, "Table A2: Building emissions, all estimators")

## ---------- Appendix Table A3: robustness ----------

key_main <- c(urb = "urb_rate", prim = "population_largest_city_pct_urb", m1 = "pop_over_1M_pct_urb")
key_lag  <- c(urb = "lag_urb_rate", prim = "lag_population_largest_city_pct_urb", m1 = "lag_pop_over_1M_pct_urb")
key_alt  <- c(urb = "urb_rate", prim = "population_largest_city_pct_urb", m1 = "urban_population_over_1M")
key_ld   <- setNames(paste0("d_", key_main), names(key_main))
term_map_rob <- list(key_main, key_main, key_lag, key_alt, key_main, key_ld)

rob_cols <- names(r_tr)   # Baseline, Driscoll-Kraay SE, lagged, LAS as % of total pop., excl. 4 countries

rob_panel <- function(r, ld, title) {
  ms <- c(r[rob_cols], list(ld))
  vs <- c(robust_vcov(r)[rob_cols], list(vcovHC(ld, type = "HC1")))
  names(ms) <- names(vs) <- paste0("c", 1:6)
  list(rows = bind_rows(panel_row(title, names(ms)),
                        reg_block(ms, vs, names(lab3), lab3, term_map_rob)),
       nobs = map_int(ms, nobs))
}

rA <- rob_panel(r_tr, m_ld[["Transport"]], "Panel A: Transport")
rB <- rob_panel(r_bu, m_ld[["Buildings"]], "Panel B: Buildings")
cols_rob <- paste0("c", 1:6)

t_rob <- bind_rows(
  rA$rows, rB$rows,
  stat_row("Controls",            rep("Yes", 6), cols_rob),
  stat_row("Country and year FE", c(rep("Yes", 5), "–"), cols_rob),
  stat_row("Observations",        rA$nobs, cols_rob)
)
n_coef_rob <- nrow(rA$rows) + nrow(rB$rows)

ft_rob <- flextable(t_rob) |>
  set_header_labels(values = list(Variable = "", c1 = "Baseline", c2 = "Driscoll–Kraay SE",
                                  c3 = "Lagged (t−1)", c4 = "LAS as % of total pop.",
                                  c5 = "Excl. 4 countries", c6 = "Long differences")) |>
  add_header_row(values = c("", paste0("(", 1:6, ")")), colwidths = rep(1, 7)) |>
  style_booktabs(
    caption = "Table A3: Robustness checks for the urban-structure coefficients",
    widths = c(1.65, 0.72, 0.72, 0.72, 0.8, 0.72, 0.88),
    note = paste("Dependent variable: ln per capita CO₂ emissions of the sector.",
                 "Controls: ln household consumption p.c. and ln population density.",
                 "(1) Two-way FE, SE clustered by country (as in Table 3).",
                 "(2) Same model with Driscoll–Kraay SE (2 lags), which may understate uncertainty with T = 20.",
                 "(3) Urban-structure variables lagged by one year; the year 2000 is lost (N = 665).",
                 "(4) LAS measured as % of total population (original World Bank measure).",
                 "(5) Excludes TUR, JPN, NLD and CRI (suspected changes in national urban definitions).",
                 "(6) Long differences between 2000–02 and 2017–19 averages, one observation per country, HC1 robust SE.",
                 STARS_NOTE),
    panel_i = c(1, nrow(rA$rows) + 1),
    rule_i  = c(nrow(rA$rows), n_coef_rob))
ft_rob

## ---------- Appendix Table A4: industry placebo ----------

body_plac <- reg_block(m_plac, map(m_plac, vc_cl), x_main, labels)
t_plac <- bind_rows(
  body_plac,
  stat_row("Country and year FE", rep("Yes", 3), names(m_plac)),
  stat_row("Observations",        map_int(m_plac, nobs), names(m_plac)),
  stat_row("R²",                  fmt_num(map_dbl(m_plac, r2_of)), names(m_plac))
)
ft_plac <- flextable(t_plac) |>
  set_header_labels(values = list(Variable = "", c1 = "Transport", c2 = "Buildings", c3 = "Industry (placebo)")) |>
  style_booktabs(
    caption = "Table A4: Placebo test with industrial emissions",
    note = paste("Two-way FE; dependent variables are ln per capita CO₂ emissions of each sector.",
                 "The transport and buildings columns are the main estimates of Table 3.",
                 "Industrial combustion is a placebo outcome with no direct link to urban structure.",
                 "Standard errors clustered by country in parentheses.", STARS_NOTE),
    rule_i = nrow(body_plac))
ft_plac

## ---------- Export: one .docx per table ----------

thesis_tables <- list(table2_descriptives      = ft_desc,
                      table3_main_results      = ft_main,
                      table4_tests             = ft_tests,
                      table5_within_between    = ft_wb,
                      tableA1_transport_all    = ft_A1,
                      tableA2_buildings_all    = ft_A2,
                      tableA3_robustness       = ft_rob,
                      tableA4_placebo          = ft_plac)

iwalk(thesis_tables, ~ save_as_docx(.x, path = out_thesis(paste0(.y, ".docx"))))
```
